archetypes.name: oos-env-handoff
archetypes.rationale: The emit-tally skip guard pivots on OOS_ACCEPTED_COUNT from review-tally.env, but the plan does not detail when and how tally writes that key — if the counter is written before normalization or defaults to 0, the guard silently fails and oos-serialize still overwrites.
archetypes.prompt_body: Verify in tally-code-votes.sh and emit-tally.sh that OOS_ACCEPTED_COUNT is written to review-tally.env after all normalization and append operations complete, so the count reflects actual blocks written. Check whether count_from_tally correctly defaults to 0 when the key is absent versus when the file itself is absent, and confirm that the skip guard fires for a tally run that normalized legacy FINDING_ headers rather than only for runs that already carried OOS_ headers. Confirm that the guard cannot be bypassed if tally is re-run with an empty accepted file after emit-tally already preserved a prior normalized file. Verify the test-emit-tally.sh cases explicitly assert that OOS_ACCEPTED_COUNT is non-zero when the pre-seeded tally output is present, not just that the file is unchanged. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: unscoped-oos-consumers
archetypes.rationale: The bug description names parse-input.sh, oos-serialize.sh, accumulated-oos.md, and oos-accepted-main-agent.md as relevant paths but none appear in scope-files; the plan relies on producer normalization making them safe to skip, a claim that requires evidence from actual file content.
archetypes.prompt_body: Examine whether parse-input.sh (OOS issue filing), oos-serialize.sh, oos-disposition-checkpoint.sh, and any script reading oos-accepted-review.md or accumulated-oos.md depend on the canonical ### OOS_N: schema and would silently fail or miscount if a legacy FINDING_ header survived. For each unscoped consumer, verify that producer normalization in tally-code-votes.sh is guaranteed to execute before that consumer runs in every production code path, or document why the consumer is unreachable for this fix. Check whether the issue description's suggestion to mirror normalization in oos-accepted-main-agent.md and design OOS producers is correctly deferred or inadvertently left as a latent gap. Confirm that accumulated-oos.md — which the bug description mentions but the plan does not address — cannot accumulate un-normalized FINDING_ headers across review rounds that would re-introduce the silent-drop on a subsequent gate evaluation. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
